Two other plants were caught. A2 replays the earlier round's resolve_login lookup endpoint and failed 3 tests: the source gate, the HTTP attack and a self-test. Every G2 test passes in ./erp verify: fallback deny, exactly one permission or reviewed anonymous, no-roles user denied everything, grant escalation on create and update, and list permission checks. The e2e test 'a user whose roles grant nothing sees no menu' passes.

P2 replays the earlier round's plant, which removes RoleGrants.WithinCaller from POST /api/identity/users. It was caught by 3 tests (Creating_a_user_cannot_grant_more_than_the_caller_holds, No_endpoint_grants_more_than_the_caller_holds and a self-test), so the round 1 gap stays fixed. P3 adds POST /api/identity/users/{id}/deactivate with RequireAuthorization() only. The host refused to start ('declares no permission') and all 45 gate tests failed (plants/plant-p3-no-permission.log).

biggest_gap.title: The G1 gate misses a cross-tenant leak through shared process state, such as a static or singleton cache
biggest_gap.detail: The G1 HTTP attack only ever signs in tenant A's users. Tenant B never sends a request to the app under test, so B's data never enters process-wide state: static fields, singletons, IMemoryCache, output caching, or anything keyed without the tenant. In production both tenants share one process, so this whole class of leak can ship. I added a 3-line static cache to GET /api/tenancy/tenant. The gate suite (45/45) and the full .NET suite (126/126) still pass, while tenant A's admin receives tenant B's tenant record. The gate needs B (and A) to be active at the same time: drive B's users through every GET and write first, interleave them with A's attack, then look for B's markers in A's responses and the reverse. A self-test should plant a static cache to prove the gate catches it.
biggest_gap.evidence: Reproduce: `git apply gauntlet/evidence/p01-odoo-rig/r1/plants/plant-a4-static-cache.diff && dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release`, which reports 'Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 45' (plants/plant-a4-static-cache.log). The full `dotnet test Erp.slnx -c Release` also passes (plants/plant-a4-full-dotnet-suite.log). Proof of the leak: apply plants/plant-a4-proof.diff (it adds SelfTests/CriticPlantProof.cs) and run with --filter CriticPlantProof. The test signs in gulfsteel's admin, then alnoor's admin, and asserts alnoor's GET /api/tenancy/tenant contains gulfsteel's tenant id. It passes (plants/plant-a4-proof.log). Script: plants/run-plants.sh.

other_findings: Instrument bias against the reference (create-restricted-user): Tab from the Odoo name field lands in the login field, but the driver clicks it. The form also has an Alt+S save hotkey. Odoo's modelled human seconds (37.03) are therefore overstated by about 2 s, so a later 'win' on human seconds could be an artefact. The six driver paths were never checked as the shortest for each metric (probes/probe-odoo-paths.json).

switch-to-arabic is measured as lang.tester, who has only base.group_user. In this rig that user has no apps and lands on an empty client before and after the switch. The blind start and done screenshots show no Arabic text, and Odoo reloads an empty client, so machine seconds are understated (probes/probe-lang-tester-landing.json, screenshots 06 and 07). Use a user with a real working screen, such as Contacts.

There is no way to load the shared dataset (gauntlet/compare/data: contacts.csv, users.csv, rates.csv) into our product. `./erp up` seeds its own 100,000 users (for example abdullah.aldhaheri.10768@alnoor.example), not users.csv. The 'both products hold the same records' promise, and needle uniqueness, are enforced only on the Odoo side.

The one command never re-verifies the six Odoo baselines. verify-inside.sh excludes live-odoo.test.mjs, so verify runs 45 harness tests. The ratchet's compare.harnessTests=47 is counted by grepping `^test(` in source, so it includes 2 live tests that never run in ./erp verify.

Blindness leaks: review.html captions show driver-specific moment names ('labels in Arabic, layout still left to right', 'mapping preview'), and result JSONs carry vendor UI step labels ('Edit Properties', 'Approve Order'). The vendor-name placeholder mask also paints over the contact's Website value with a grey box, which singles out the reference product.

The plan names a comparison task for every piece (sign in, create company and branch, switch company, keyboard navigation, edit and save, Arabic report, who changed this field, add a rate, configure a sequence, attach and find a file, see and rerun a job, export a filtered list, an API task). None is defined yet. Every task starts already signed in, so p00's 'sign in' comparison still cannot be measured. The rig already loads 100,000 audit messages, attachments, job runs and rates for these tasks.

Rig realism: the 100,000 attachments share 8 stored blobs. Cloned audit message bodies do not match the contacts' real e-mails (screenshot 02 shows 'old73518@... → new73518@...' on contact 73519). ir.cron.progress rows decay after a week unless up.sh is run again (documented).
Approver and buyer sign-ins for the rig are hard-coded in gauntlet/compare/lib/config.mjs and cannot be overridden from the environment, unlike admin.

Positive: the rig is reproducible and idempotent under my own project and port (161 s from empty, 11 s on a second run). Counts checked directly in the rig database: 100,000 dataset contacts, 100,003 active internal users, 100,000 rates across 50 currencies, 100,007 tracking messages, 100,046 contact attachments, 100,001 cron progress rows, 100,000 purchase orders (200 to approve), and en_US plus ar_001 active. All six Odoo drivers verified three times with step and keystroke counts identical to the committed baselines.
